title: Sermon on the Dormition of the Most Holy Theotokos
attribution_note: Translated for this edition from the Russian of St Theophan the Recluse (public domain), his sermon on the Dormition of our Most Holy Lady the Theotokos and Ever-Virgin Mary. The Russian text the translation was made from is kept in the repository.

pairs.en: After the death of Jesus Christ on the Cross, His Most Pure Mother lived for about fifteen years in Jerusalem, in the house of the holy Apostle John the Theologian, to whose care the Lord Himself had entrusted her from the Cross. Now the time drew near for her to pass to the heavenly dwelling of her Son. While the Mother of God was praying on the Mount of Olives, the Archangel Gabriel appeared to her, tradition tells us, bringing a palm branch, and announced that her repose would come in three days.

The Most Pure Virgin rejoiced beyond words at this news, and began to prepare. By the day of her passing, at God's command, all the apostles were miraculously gathered to Jerusalem — all but Thomas — scattered as they were across the whole world in their preaching. They were witnesses of her peaceful, quiet, holy and blessed repose. The Lord Jesus Christ Himself, in heavenly glory, surrounded by a countless host of angels and righteous spirits, appeared to receive the soul of His Most Pure Mother, and with glory raised her up to heaven.

So did the Most Holy Virgin Mary end her earthly life! With lighted lamps and the singing of psalms, the apostles carried the body of the Mother of God to Gethsemane, where her parents and Joseph were buried. The unbelieving chief priests and scribes, struck by the grandeur of the funeral procession and embittered by the honor being paid to the Mother of God, sent servants and soldiers to scatter those accompanying her and to burn the body of the Mother of God itself.

The crowd, roused to fury, and the soldiers with them, rushed at the Christians — but were struck blind. At that moment the Jewish priest Athonius happened to be passing by. He threw himself at the bier, meaning to overturn it to the ground; but no sooner had he laid his hands on it than an angel cut off both his hands. The severed hands hung there at the bier, and Athonius himself fell to the ground, crying out.

The Apostle Peter halted the procession and said to Athonius: *“Be assured that Christ is the true God.”* Athonius at once confessed Christ as the true Messiah. The Apostle Peter told him to turn to the Mother of God in fervent prayer, and to press what remained of his hands to the severed parts hanging at the bier. When he did so, his hands were joined together again and healed, and only the marks of the cutting remained. The blinded people and soldiers, in repentance, touched the bier, and received their sight — not only of the body, but of the soul — and all of them, in reverence, joined the procession.

On the third day after the burial of the Mother of God, the Apostle Thomas, who had been kept away by God's will, arrived, and wished to see her tomb. At his request the tomb was opened — but the body of the Mother of God was not found in it.

That same evening, as the apostles sat at table, they saw the Most Holy Virgin in the air above them, alive, in the heavens, with a multitude of angels. The Mother of God, standing there, shining with ineffable glory, said to the apostles: *“Rejoice!* *I am always with you.”* And the apostles cried out: *“Most Holy Theotokos, help us.”* This appearance of the Mother of God convinced the apostles completely — and through them, the whole Church — of her resurrection.

In imitation of the Most Holy Virgin Mary, who so often visited the places that her Son and God had sanctified with the steps of His most pure feet, there arose among Christians the custom of making pilgrimage to holy places.
